The circle is divided into three sectors, one for each type of economy, and each sector has four places - the name of the economy, the ownership and management of the means of production, the main aim, and the countries that have adopted it. Filling the nine '?' places gives:

| Point | Capitalistic Economy | Socialistic Economy | Mixed Economy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ownership and management of the means of production | Management in private hands, that is, in the hands of private individuals | The means of production belong to the society as a whole, i.e. under the government's control | Co-existence of private and public sectors |
| Main aim | To earn maximum profit | Achieving social welfare | A balance between profit and social welfare is made |
| Countries that have adopted it | Germany, Japan, the USA | China and Russia | India, Sweden and United Kingdom |

Of these twelve entries, three were already printed in the circle - 'Management in private hands' in the capitalistic sector, 'Achieving social welfare' in the socialistic sector and 'India, Sweden and United Kingdom' in the mixed sector. The other nine are the ones filled in above.

The word 'economics' comes from the Greek word 'oikonomia', which means 'family management'. Every family has a certain income and many needs to meet out of it, so it has to decide its preferences and strike a balance between its income and its expenditure. This management of individual or family finances is mainly related to income and expenditure, that is, to economic factors, and it is from this that economics was born. There is a lot of similarity between family management and economics. Just as we manage the finances of our family, villages and cities, states, countries and the world also need economic management. In this sense economy begins at home.

India has adopted the mixed type of economy. In a mixed economy the private sector and the public sector co-exist, so the means of production are neither wholly in private hands nor wholly under the government's control. Its working aim is also mixed - a balance is made between earning profit and achieving social welfare. Sweden and the United Kingdom have adopted the same type of system as India.

The enterprises related to the production, distribution and consumption of goods and services in a specific region are called an economy. On a global level there are three types of economies, so on the basis of the economy they follow, countries can be divided into three groups. In a capitalistic economy the ownership and management of the means of production is in the hands of private individuals and the main aim is to earn maximum profit; Germany, Japan and the USA have adopted this type. In a socialistic economy the means of production belong to the society as a whole, i.e. they are under the government's control, and the main aim is to achieve social welfare; China and Russia have adopted this type. In a mixed economy the private and public sectors co-exist and a balance is made between profit and social welfare; India, Sweden and the United Kingdom have adopted this type.
It is mainly related to income and expenditure, that is, to economic factors.

Globalisation means building a world economy, that is, aligning the country's economy with the world economy, so that trade is free, restrictions on investments are set aside, and natural resources, profit, services, capital, labour and technology flow freely across the borders of countries.
